title: Verifier-Guided Prompting for Intent-to-Configuration Translation: A Preregistered NetOps Study
abstract: We preregistered and executed a paired confirmatory trial to test whether constrained prompting combined with a deterministic verifier-guided generate→verify→repair loop (one allowed repair) increases deterministic-verifier semantic-correctness when translating operator natural-language intents into low-level device configurations. Design: N=150 synthetic intents from a deterministic generator, shared_initial_candidate execution semantics, model = gpt-5-mini, deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, one initial generation per intent shared across baseline and guarded conditions, guarded pipeline permitted ≤1 repair call. Results (artifact-grounded): baseline = 149/150 (99.333%); guarded = 150/150 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.006667 (≈0.67 percentage points); exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap percentile CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729). Provider accounting: completed episodes = 300; model_calls_used = 151; repair-stage invocations = 1. Interpretation: on this preregistered synthetic corpus and under shared_initial_candidate semantics the guarded workflow produced a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. We highlight a methodological lesson: preregistered NetOps trials require baseline-calibration pilots to avoid ceiling effects that invalidate preregistered power assumptions. All execution and analysis artifacts are archived in the execution bundle referenced by the execution manifest.

sections.introduction:
Natural-language intent interfaces promise to reduce operator burden by letting humans express desired network changes as free text that is automatically translated into executable device configurations. Prior work reports that single-pass LLM outputs often contain syntactic errors, omissions, or semantic violations that can yield unsafe or unavailable states if applied directly [1][2][3]. A common defensive architecture is generate→verify→repair: an LLM produces a candidate, a deterministic verifier checks intent-level invariants or formalized constraints, and an automated repair (or human gate) corrects violations before execution [4][5]. Security analyses further motivate deterministic gating because unvetted textual claims can become harmful tool calls in multi-tool agentic workflows [6].

Research question. After an autonomous literature review and preregistration we posed a confined confirmatory question: does constrained prompting (structured templates with explicit semantic slots) combined with deterministic verifier-guided iterative feedback materially increase verifier-level semantic correctness of NL→configuration translation versus an unconstrained baseline under a paired design? The trial (study_cand_2026_b2_v1) was preregistered and frozen before any model outputs were observed.

Contributions. (1) A fully preregistered, artifactized paired confirmatory trial measuring deterministic-verifier pass/fail on a programmatically generated synthetic corpus (N=150 paired intents). (2) Artifact-backed outcomes showing that, under shared_initial_candidate semantics and a one-repair budget, the guarded pipeline raised verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (+0.67 pp), a numerically negligible and statistically non-significant improvement (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). (3) A methodological recommendation that preregistered NetOps trials include baseline-calibration pilots and explicitly specify generation semantics (shared_initial_candidate vs independent sampling) because semantics materially change the estimand and interpretation.
sections.related_work:
Related literature spans intent-translation evaluations, verifier-guided repair systems, formal verifier tooling, and agentic/tool-augmented safety analyses. Recent NL→configuration and intent-to-configuration studies document translation challenges: free-text prompts frequently produce omissions or incorrect sequencing that violate required invariants, and benchmark studies report modest semantic-correctness rates on heterogeneous task banks [1].

Work that integrates deterministic verification into generation workflows reports improved practical correctness, but gains depend on baseline competence, verifier expressiveness, and repair budget. Policy-guided verifier feedback and verifier-in-the-loop fine-tuning (e.g., TerraFormer, IaC efforts) demonstrate that verifier signals can rerank or guide repairs for infrastructure-as-code artifacts, reducing syntactic and semantic errors [2]. Independent benchmarks for configuration repair also show generate→verify→repair pipelines can improve validity, with effect sizes varying by sampling semantics (single-shot vs multi-sample), repair allowance, and verifier feedback format [3].

Deterministic formal-verification tools (NetKAT/KATch family and related engines) can serve as concrete oracles for reachability, isolation, and high-level policy checks and are commonly proposed as gating layers for LLM-generated configurations [5]. Security and systems analyses of agentic LLM pipelines warn that unguarded multi-tool agents can convert false textual claims into harmful actions and are susceptible to prompt-injection and claim-to-action exploit patterns; these studies motivate designs that make verifier verdicts explicit, auditable, and conservative for ambiguous intents [4]. Our trial operationalizes a narrowly constrained guarded architecture and emphasizes preregistration, paired inference, and deterministic-verifier endpoints, while explicitly controlling two operational knobs identified in prior work: repair budget and sampling semantics [2][3][5][6].
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory design. The study was preregistered as study_cand_2026_b2_v1 with a frozen analysis plan executed before any model outputs were observed. The preregistration conceptualized three conditions: A) baseline (free-text prompt), B) constrained-template prompting (structured template + semantic slots), and C) constrained + verifier-feedback (generate→verify→repair). The preregistered hypotheses were H1: constrained (B) improves over baseline (A), and H2: guarded (C) improves over constrained (B).

Mapping preregistration labels to the executed contrast (required reviewer correction). The archived execution adapter enforced shared_initial_candidate semantics and a strict call budget (exactly one initial model generation per intent, and at most one additional guarded repair call). Under those adapter constraints the actual paired confirmatory estimand executed and archived is the contrast C vs A under shared_initial_candidate semantics: for each intent a single initial sampled candidate was produced and that identical candidate was evaluated as the baseline (A) and then (if failed) subjected to at most one guarded repair (C). Consequently: (a) the preregistered conceptual labels H1/H2 and the three-condition plan remain as specified in the preregistration, but (b) the registered and archived confirmatory test reported here is C vs A under shared_initial_candidate semantics. The constrained-only condition B was not executed as an independent first-pass sampling arm in the adapter-enforced run and therefore no independent B-vs-A or C-vs-B confirmatory contrasts are reported in the archived analysis artifacts. This explicit mapping is reported here to avoid any implication that independent per-condition first-pass sampling occurred.

Execution semantics and adapter enforcement. Execution semantics were enforced by the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter: for each intent the adapter created exactly one shared initial model call (shared_initial_generation = 150) and, only if the deterministic verifier failed that candidate, permitted at most one repair call (repair invocations observed = 1). Provider accounting recorded model_calls_used = 151 and completed_episode_count = 300, consistent with the registered shared_initial_candidate semantics and the one-repair budget.

Model and deterministic validator. Declared model: gpt-5-mini (provider record: openai_responses). The archived model_configuration.json records declared_model_version = "gpt-5-mini" and temperature = null (unset); because no numeric temperature or fixed random-seed was enforced, independent API sessions may yield nondeterministic outputs. Deterministic verifier: deterministic_netops_validator_v5 (validator_version = 5.0) applied the full_intent_constraint_validation rule and returned a pass/fail verdict plus normalized final-configuration text and diagnostics. These binary verifier verdicts were the primary confirmatory endpoint.

Tasks, inclusion/exclusion, and unit tests. Confirmatory tasks were produced deterministically by deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 and stratified across intent families (reachability/isolation, ACL-like, VLAN/MTU sequence changes, uplink switchover). Topologies were constrained to small verifier-capable networks (4–32 nodes). Parser-to-verifier mapping code and verifier-coverage unit-tests were executed before the batch; no parse failures, ambiguity-driven exclusions, or verifier-coverage exclusions occurred in this run. Inclusion/exclusion rules and the retry policy (one retry on provider timeout) were applied as preregistered.

Primary analysis and preregistered handling of pairs. The primary estimand was the paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline based on deterministic verifier pass/fail. Analysis used an exact two-sided McNemar test on the paired contingency (n_11, n_10, n_01, n_00) and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval computed with 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729). The preregistered treatment of incomplete pairs (complete_pair_primary) excluded incomplete pairs from the primary test; no incomplete pairs occurred. No post-preregistration analytic changes were made: all reported analyses follow the preregistered paired_binary_analysis_v1 executor and archived analysis scripts.
sections.results:
Execution and provider audit. The run completed as planned: completed_episode_count = 300 and complete_pair_count = 150. Provider-call accounting: model_calls_used = 151; completed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 151; failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0; cache_miss_count = 151. Stage-level counts: shared_initial_generation = 150 and repair = 1. No contamination flags or pre-execution unit-test failures occurred (contamination_summary.csv empty).

Primary numerical outcomes (artifact-grounded). The paired contingency counts (guarded × baseline) were: n_11 = 149 (both-pass), n_10 = 1 (guarded-only-pass), n_01 = 0 (baseline-only-pass), n_00 = 0 (both-fail). Per-condition success rates: baseline_success_count = 149/150 = 0.9933333333333333; guarded_success_count = 150/150 = 1.0. Estimated paired absolute difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.00666666666666671 (≈0.67 percentage points). Exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.0. Paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00, 0.02] (10,000 resamples; bootstrap_seed = 1729). These values are reported verbatim from archived analysis artifacts (analysis/results.json, analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv, analysis/condition_summary.csv).

Repair diagnostics and iteration counts. Only one guarded repair invocation occurred (1/150), consistent with the near-ceiling initial success rate. That single repair converted the single initially invalid candidate to a valid configuration under the deterministic verifier. Median revision iterations for guarded episodes = 0 (IQR = 0). Validator traces include validation_before and validation_after states, parsed_command_count, required_command_count, violation_codes, and the normalized_configuration string for each episode; representative traces (tasks 000001–000006) are archived and illustrate varied difficulty patterns while confirming validator behavior.

Representative artifact example. Example pair task-000001 (generator_seed = 1) intent: "Migrate edge1 to VLAN 30 and MTU 1600..." Shared-initial and both condition responses returned the expected four-command sequence. Validator diagnostics: parsed_command_count = 4, required_command_count = 4, observed_touched_field_count = 3, valid = true. The shared-initial candidate hashes and normalized_configuration strings are archived in the execution bundle.

Sensitivity and missingness. The preregistered sensitivity analysis treating missing guarded outputs as failures was not needed: failed_hosted_model_call_event_count = 0 and unscorable episodes = 0. No exclusions or parse failures occurred.

Summary. Under the preregistered estimand (C vs A, shared_initial_candidate), the guarded workflow produced a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant improvement over a near-ceiling baseline. All numeric claims above reference archived artifact files and counts in the execution and analysis manifests.
sections.discussion:
Ceiling effect and inferential consequence. The preregistered power calculation assumed a substantially lower baseline and targeted a detectable +15 percentage-point improvement with ~80% power. The observed baseline_success_rate = 0.9933 created a ceiling effect that left almost no headroom for the guarded repair to demonstrate a large absolute improvement. With n_11 = 149 and only one discordant pair (n_10 = 1) the paired analysis contains minimal information about discordant behavior; the exact McNemar p = 1.0 and bootstrap CI containing zero indicate the archived run does not provide statistical support for a material guarded benefit under the preregistered estimand. The preregistration-prescribed analysis was followed without post-lock changes; this mismatch between assumed baseline and observed baseline reduces the study's power and motivates explicit baseline calibration in future preregistrations.

Why the synthetic corpus produced a high baseline. The deterministic generator produced tasks with explicit required_sequence constraints and tightly specified allowed_touched_fields, which reduces translation ambiguity. When intents are tightly specified and the verifier coverage matches the required invariants, a single sampled candidate from a capable LLM can often satisfy the verifier, producing a near-ceiling baseline as observed here.

Semantics, sampling, and operational trade-offs. The shared_initial_candidate semantics used here isolate the marginal effect of applying at most one repair to a fixed initial candidate. Alternative semantics—independent per-condition sampling, multi-draw ensembles, or larger repair budgets—estimate different operational questions (expected first-pass success vs re-sampling benefits) and may yield larger observable differences at the cost of additional model calls and latency. Practitioners should align sampling semantics and repair budgets with deployment constraints and include provider-call accounting in power planning.

Repair budgets, cost, and diminishing returns. Provider accounting (model_calls_used = 151; repair invocations = 1) quantifies operational cost under a one-repair design: repairs were rarely invoked at near-ceiling baseline, so marginal cost per observed success-gain is high. In lower-baseline scenarios repairs convert more failures but additional repairs show diminishing returns; quantifying that frontier requires multi-arm experiments varying repair budgets, which we did not run in this confirmatory trial but which the archived seeds and code can reproduce.

Operational affordances beyond binary pass/fail. The deterministic validator produces normalized configurations, parsed command counts, and explicit violation codes that aid human triage and automated repair design even when marginal verifier-pass gains are small. Guarded pipelines therefore offer operational observability and auditable artifacts beyond the single binary endpoint.

Threats to validity and limitations (summary). Internal validity: adapter-enforced budgets and provider audits mitigate cross-condition leakage; mapping unit-tests reduced parser failures. Construct validity: deterministic verifier pass/fail is a proxy for semantic correctness and depends on mapping code and verifier coverage. External validity: single declared model (gpt-5-mini) and synthetic small topologies (4–32 nodes) limit generalization to production-scale heterogeneous networks. Security/adversarial robustness: this trial did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection; separate adversary-driven experiments are needed. Conclusion validity: the baseline mismatch to preregistered power assumptions underscores the need for pilot calibration to preserve inferential validity.

Practical prescriptions. We recommend (1) a short baseline-calibration pilot (e.g., 20–40 tasks) to estimate baseline_success_rate and discordant-pair proportions before fixing N; (2) explicit preregistration of sampling semantics and repair budgets; (3) multi-arm designs that vary repair budgets and sampling semantics to estimate cost–benefit trade-offs; (4) inclusion of provider-call accounting in power calculations; and (5) staged scaling of verifier coverage with deterministic unit-tests for mapping code. The archived manifests and representative tasks provide concrete seeds and runnable code for these prescriptions.
sections.conclusion: We executed a fully preregistered paired confirmatory trial comparing baseline free-text prompting with constrained-template prompting plus a single verifier-guided repair under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a deterministic synthetic corpus with gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5, the guarded pipeline increased verifier pass rate from 149/150 to 150/150 (≈0.67 pp), a numerically tiny and statistically non-significant difference (exact McNemar p = 1.0; 95% bootstrap CI = [0.00, 0.02]). The principal scientific lesson is methodological: preregistered NetOps trials should include baseline calibration to avoid ceiling effects and preserve statistical power. Technically, our artifacts bound the marginal benefit of a one-repair guarded pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics; evaluating independent-sampling semantics, larger repair budgets, model diversity, and production-scale topologies remains important future work.

limitations: Single-model constraint: experiments used only gpt-5-mini; results do not generalize across models or sizes.

Synthetic corpus and scale: tasks were programmatically generated and limited to verifier-capable toy-to-small topologies (4–32 nodes); external validity to production WANs and heterogeneous vendor CLIs is untested.

Shared_initial_candidate semantics and execution contract limited repair budget to at most one guarded repair call per intent; different generation semantics or multiple-repair budgets may yield different outcomes.

Ceiling effect and preregistration mismatch: baseline correctness was far higher than the pilot assumptions used for power calculations (planned detectable effect = 15 percentage points), reducing the trial's ability to demonstrate benefit and illustrating sensitivity to baseline calibration.

Verifier coverage and specification translation: the study measures deterministic validator pass/fail on the preregistered invariants but does not claim safety guarantees beyond the deterministic validator's modeled properties.

Security and adversarial robustness: the experiment did not evaluate adversarial prompt-injection or adversary-driven intents; separate targeted studies are required to assess claim-to-action vulnerabilities in agentic NetOps workflows.
